adjudications.rationale: Package manifest contains unversioned direct URL Git dependencies. Violates zero-trust unpinned dependency policy in strict enterprise environments, though not actively malicious.
Legitimate diagnostic utility monkeypatching process deprecation event emitters. Flagged by aggressive heuristic rule.

EJS inherently functions as a dynamic JavaScript runtime, compiling template strings into executable JS via Function constructors. While by design, EJS official security policy explicitly warns that passing untrusted user input to render options is inherently unsafe. Under a zero-trust execution sink gate, blocking this capability is a correct risk decision, distinct from asserting an unpatched CVE.
Pure HTTP header freshness validator with zero dangerous sinks. Genuine scanner false positive.

Contains code generation via Function constructor in lib/js-yaml/type/js/function.js (supporting !!js/function schema type). While historical CVE-2013-4660 formally applied to v2.x and subsequent v3.14.1 vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-64718 prototype pollution, CVE-2026-59869 quadratic complexity) differ in mechanism, the active code path constructing functions from text is an inherently dangerous deserialization pattern justified for policy blocking.
Dynamic compilation of log format strings into functions. Benign metaprogramming safe in standard Express deployment.
Glob matching library containing direct dependency references. Policy-level gate enforcement.
Test spec test/basic_auth_spec.js defines dummy test credentials ('user:pass') for HTTP basic auth test assertions. Block is context-dependent due to absence of test-path exclusion.
Dynamically instruments Error.prepareStackTrace to map stack traces. Benign developer tooling.
Virtual file format containing direct repository references. Supply-chain policy enforcement.
Triggers on aggressive postinstall lifecycle script patterns combined with dynamic function arity construction. Blocking unverified lifecycle scripts is justified supply-chain defense.
